summary: Connection handoff livelock between API gateway and runtime causing elevated 5xx error-rate
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChime reported a sudden rise in 5xx responses from our hosted inference endpoint for dedicated tenants in us-east. Error rate started at ~00:42 UTC and sustained a ~6% 5xx error-rate for ~45 minutes.

Impact:
- BrightChime experienced degraded API success rate for synchronous chat generation (multi-turn).
- Overall platform 5xx floor in us-east increased from 0.2% -> 6% for the window.
- Latency P95 climbed modestly (120ms -> 240ms) before the 5xx wave.

Timeline (high level):
- 00:41 UTC: first alert from healthcheck and customer complaint via email.
- 00:42 UTC: apigw error-rate alert (5xx > 4%).
- 00:44 UTC: on-call support triaged to Sev1 and paged runtime on-call.
- 00:50 UTC: initial mitigation applied (temporary tightening of per-tenant concurrency).
- 01:25 UTC: error-rate began to subside after targeted priority-shed tuning and proxy queue drain.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Fire a steady stream of short-payload requests (avg payload 350 bytes) from a single tenant at ~80 RPS pinned to dedicated pool.
2. After a few seconds, apigw accept queue grows and handoff completion latency increases.
3. Runtime starts returning 5xx (502/503) as handoff timeouts and worker preemption is observed.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- apigw: "handoff_wait_ms > 250" spike correlated with 5xx increases.
- proxy-handoff: repeated "handoff-livelock: attempt_requeue" traces with backlog > 500.
- runtime: intermittent "worker-preempt: evicting request due to preemption" and periodic OOM_ksoftirq-like logs in NVML metrics.
- scheduler: elevated backpressure events and priority-shed activations.

Initial hypothesis:
The apigw->proxy handoff path and the runtime accept/worker handshake entered a pathological loop: when proxy sees longer handoff latencies it requeues connections; requeueing increases queue length and amplifies handoff latency, which in turn causes the runtime scheduler to preempt workers (priority-shed) and drop inflight requests. This creates a livelock where short, high-frequency requests keep cycling through the accept/handoff logic until backpressure and priority-shed escalate into visible 5xx.

Why this is unique/different from prior 5xx waves:
- Root cause appears localized to handoff coordination and requeueing logic rather than pure GPU OOM or kernel fallback.
- Pattern shows strong sensitivity to short-payload high-RPS tenants pinned to dedicated pool with aggressive keepalive reuse.
investigation_notes: 00:46 UTC - Support: collected apigw accept queue histograms and handoff latency distribution from edge nodes.
00:48 UTC - Runtime on-call: captured worker thread dumps and NVML memory allocation delta for affected runtimes.
00:52 UTC - Observed correlation: handoff_wait_ms tail aligned with apigw 5xx spikes across 4 edge nodes serving BrightChime traffic.
00:58 UTC - Hypothesis refined: requeue policy in proxy-handoff backpressure path is too aggressive for short-lived multiplexed connections, causing accept queue thrash.
01:05 UTC - Tested mitigation: increased requeue_delay_ms and lowered immediate-requeue threshold on a canary edge node; observed local error-rate drop from 7% -> 1.2% within 3 minutes.
01:20 UTC - Confirmed fix path: roll change to requeue_delay_ms to 50ms and adjust accept-queue-watermarks in apigw config; applied to 30% of edges with monitoring.
Follow-up owners assigned: proxy team to harden requeue heuristics (PR linked), runtime team to add backpressure metrics and a non-preemptive slow-path for short requests.
Mitigation was coordinated with BrightChime CS to throttle their burst concurrency as temporary relief while we rolled config changes.

resolution:
Mitigations applied: (1) Adjusted proxy requeue heuristic (requeue_delay_ms increased, immediate_requeue_threshold raised) and rolled to production edges incrementally. (2) Temporary per-tenant concurrency cap applied to BrightChime while rollout completed. (3) Runtime change to avoid preemptive eviction for requests under 1KB implemented in PR #2145 and will be staged. Error-rate returned to baseline after rollout.

Follow-up actions (post-incident):
- Proxy team to land hardened requeue algorithm and add unit/integration tests for handoff edge cases (owner: Maya).
- Runtime team to instrument backpressure and add a non-preemptive slow-path for short requests (owner: Ravi).
- DX/Support to update runbook with steps for triaging handoff-livelock and a temporary tenant-throttle template (owner: Eleanor).
- Schedule a postmortem meeting and publish to Confluence by 2026-03-16.
